WINE LIS
H A
Champagne is both a place and a method. The place is north of Paris. The method is what puts
the bubbles into still wine. The French will insist that Champagne can be made only in the place
of that name: others think otherwise. It is a question for lawyers to decide. The French also will insist
that champagne from Champagne is inimitable. and that is less debatable.
BRUT PREMIER
Roederer Brut Premier
Louis Roederer is one of the smaller export houses
of Champagne, and one of the most famous. Deep
gold hues hint at the riches Brut Premier delivers. A
high proportion of Pinot Noir is part of the secret.
Four years on the yeast is another.
PECIAL
•ECTION
Porto is the wine of the Upper Douro region in Northern Portugal. It is fortified by the addition of grape
brandy which stops the fermentation and leaves behind residual sugar: retaining some of the sweetness.
Only the fortified wine from Portugal, and not its copies, can be designated Porto.
Cockburn's Special Reserve Porto
In this classic wood port, a faintly ambered.
slightly pale ruby hue reveals the presence of aged
blending stocks and a proportion of white grapes.
included to provide rounded textures and mature
flavors at bottling. Cockburn (pronounced Coe-
burn) is one of many Port firms founded by Brit-
ons. hence the name.
